title: Four-four rhythm and getting punch
summary: Allen asks how players get the New Orleans rhythm; DeVore says four-four and punch matter more than notes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I mean, there certainly is a definite rhythm.
Well, yeah. And do you get that from records or do you get that
from studying with a guy or do you get it from sitting in or what?

Well, for a New Orleans style band, the most important thing as far as rhythm is concerned is you're playing four-four time rather than two beat or any other times that bands have played. And the rhythm angle is the most important of all. I mean, even if a guy couldn't play a lick on a piano or a cornet, just make a few notes if he did it with punch. That would represent more jazz feeling than a guy that could rip off a whole slew of notes and stuff from the strictly legitimate end. So you aim for punch, huh? Yeah.
